Title: Zetrix offers RM100mil upfront, 6-month instalments to settle RTD arrears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd has offered to pay RM100 million upfront to be reappointed as a Road Transport Department (RTD) revenue collection agent, with the remaining RM214 million in arrears to be settled over six months.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah told the Dewan Rakyat today that the proposal had been referred to the Finance Ministry, while a RM29 million penalty had been imposed on the company under the terms of its agreement.
He said Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, submitted the proposal in a letter to the Transport Ministry dated Nov 5.
The remaining RM214 million would be paid in 6 equal monthly instalments of RM35.67 million. The ministry forwarded the proposal to the Finance Ministry on Nov 10.
"The total penalty imposed is RM29 million based on the terms and conditions of the agreement," he said.
My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MYEG Group,
failed to remit
RM314 million in government revenue collected between May 19 and Sept 30.
The RTD
suspended both companies
as its collection agents effective Oct 5.
Explaining why the company had been given more time, Hasbi said it had repeatedly committed to settling the outstanding revenue after receiving reminder letters.
He said extensions were granted because the company was still providing services and the government wanted to avoid disruptions.
These included online payment of summonses by foreigners at Malaysia-Singapore border entry points and computerised theory test centres in Sabah and Sarawak, as e-testing was only expected to be fully available by 2028.
Hasbi said MyEG handled 61.16 per cent of collections through collection agents and 13.27 per cent of the department's total revenue as at Sept 30.
He added that the ministry's legal adviser had taken steps to issue a notice of demand, with court action to follow if payment was not made within the stipulated period, after consultation with the Attorney-General's Chambers.
However, he said the notice and court action would not proceed if the government accepted Zetrix AI's settlement proposal.
An MP later questioned the proposal to reappoint the company as a collection agent as part of the arrangement to recover its outstanding payments.
Hasbi replied that the proposal was now with the Finance Ministry for consideration.
On Oct 27, then transport minister Anthony Loke said
full settlement
of all outstanding payments, including late-transfer penalties, was a precondition for any extension or further operational consideration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar welcomes Indonesia's commitment to tackling transboundary haze
Article:
MANILA: Malaysia and other Asean member states have welcomed Indonesia's commitment to addressing the issue of transboundary haze.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the issue was raised by Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto himself during the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits today.
Acknowledging the complexity of the issue, Anwar said he was optimistic that Indonesia's approach would yield positive results.
"President Prabowo took the initiative to raise the issue of haze and its impact on neighbouring countries. We said we were ready to cooperate, and he outlined the measures being taken.
"We acknowledge that the issue is complex and difficult to resolve, but we are pleased with Indonesia's commitment and cooperation with Asean countries to, if not prevent it entirely, at least reduce its impact in the future," said Anwar at a press conference here.
Anwar said Malaysia and other neighbouring countries, including Singapore, were also encouraged by the development and had pledged to continue assisting Indonesia in addressing the issue.
Earlier during the plenary session,
Prabowo apologised
to Malaysia and Singapore, which have been affected by transboundary haze caused by forest fires in Indonesia.
He also assured that various efforts were being undertaken to tackle the forest and land fires.
The fires in Indonesia have reportedly been burning for nearly four months, causing transboundary haze that has affected communities in Malaysia and Singapore.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's ITU Council seat opens door to early 6G discussions, says Fahmi
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia's successful bid to retain its seat on the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Council for the 2027-2030 term will give the country greater opportunities to participate in early discussions on sixth-generation (6G) communications technology and the future of global connectivity.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia's continued membership of the ITU's highest decision-making body would enable the country to play an active role in setting telecommunications standards, managing spectrum and shaping international connectivity policies.
He said Malaysia's participation was also important in sharing its experience in developing 5G networks while amplifying the voices of developing countries in global decision-making.
"I believe Malaysia's presence at this highest level, under the auspices of the United Nations, creates opportunities for us not only to share our experience in rolling out 5G and beyond.
"In fact, we now have early access to discussions on next-generation connectivity, or what is known as 6G," he said, commenting on Malaysia's next steps following its re-election to the ITU Council.
Fahmi said Malaysia's experience in developing telecommunications technology could serve as a benchmark for other countries, particularly in identifying challenges and mitigating risks at the early stages of implementation.
"This is important because our experience can serve as a lesson on what to avoid and what needs to be examined early on, while allowing developing countries to have a voice and take part in decision-making," he said.
Fahmi also thanked the teams at the Communications Ministry, the Foreign Ministry (Wisma Putra) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for their commitment to securing Malaysia's continued membership of the international body.
"I would like to congratulate everyone at the Communications Ministry, Wisma Putra and MCMC on this remarkable achievement," he said.
Malaysia retained its seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term following an election held during the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major currencies, slips against greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher against major currencies and Asean peers on Monday but weakened against the greenback as the US interest rate outlook remained hawkish.
At 6pm, the local currency eased to 4.0915/0960 versus the greenback from Friday's close of 4.0845/0890.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar remained well-supported with the US Dollar Index hovering at 103.398 points ahead of the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee meeting in December.
"The futures market has shown that the odds of a 25-basis-point rate hike have risen to more than 100 per cent. The question now is whether a 50-basis-point hike could happen at the upcoming meeting. Hence, this has led to greater demand for the US dollar," he told Bernama.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened against the euro to 4.5039/5089 from 4.5166/5216 at last Friday's close, appreciated vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3955/4014 from 5.4046/4106, but edged down against the Japanese yen to 2.5638/5666 from 2.5549/5579.
The ringgit also traded mostly higher against its Asean peers.
It rose vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 223.9/224.3 from 224.3/224.6, went up against the Philippine peso to 6.40/6.41 from 6.41/6.42, and climbed against the Thai baht to 12.0576/0755 from 12.0611/0833.
However, the local note inched down against the Singapore dollar to 3.1737/1772 from 3.1729/1769.

Title: [UPDATED] Bukit Aman verifying nationality of suspect killed in Philippines drug bust
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is verifying the nationality of a man believed to be Malaysian who was killed during a drug bust involving RM858,000 worth of methamphetamine in Tawi-Tawi, southern Philippines, yesterday.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the initial belief that the suspect was Malaysian was based on a private clinic card issued in Sabah that was found on him.
He said Philippine authorities had shared details of the incident with Malaysian police.
However, the man's nationality had yet to be confirmed as no official identification documents were found on him.
"We have been provided with details of the case by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA).
"We are working on identifying him," he said when contacted today.
The suspect, identified by Philippine authorities as Janimal Hajad, also known as "Ungod", was killed alongside his alleged Filipino accomplice, Sansibar Amirul Amil, during a buy-bust operation in Barangay Tubig Mampallam, Bongao, Tawi-Tawi.
According to the Philippine News Agency (PNA), the operation took place at 4.50pm yesterday and involved PDEA agents supported by Philippine police and marines.
PDEA Tawi-Tawi provincial officer Abraham Solon Kalim said the 2 suspects allegedly opened fire on enforcement personnel after realising they were dealing with undercover anti-narcotics agents.
The suspects reportedly attempted to escape aboard a motorised wooden boat while firing at the enforcement team.
Both men were killed in the ensuing exchange of gunfire.
Two unidentified women were also wounded by stray bullets and taken to hospital for treatment.
No casualties were reported among enforcement personnel.
Authorities seized about 2kg of suspected methamphetamine, valued at 13.4 million pesos (RM858,000), packed in two Chinese tea bags.
A pistol and the motorised wooden boat allegedly intended for the suspects' escape were also recovered.
Philippine authorities are continuing their investigation into the incident.

Title: Pos Malaysia Q3 net loss widens despite revenue growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pos Malaysia Bhd's net loss widened to RM62.25 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM45.23 million a year earlier, mainly due to one-off charges related to vessel impairments and the closure of Pos Shop.
Revenue for the quarter rose 8.3 per cent to RM501.22 million from RM462.77 million, supported by growth across all business segments.
The increase was driven by higher parcel volumes in its courier business, alongside stronger contributions from Pos Aviation, Pos Logistics and other businesses, including digital certification, data services and Pos Ar-Rahnu.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Pos Malaysia narrowed its net loss to RM125.26 million from RM132.17 million a year earlier, while revenue rose to RM1.48 billion from RM1.37 billion.
The postal segment's nine-month revenue increased 2.5 per cent to RM808.2 million, as higher parcel volumes partially offset the continued structural decline in mail volumes and retail footfall.
Its pre-tax loss narrowed to RM115.4 million from RM116.2 million.
The aviation segment recorded a 15.2 per cent increase in revenue to RM323.7 million, driven by higher cargo volumes, increased flight movements and growth in inflight catering.
Pos Logistics sustained its turnaround, with nine-month revenue rising 23.4 per cent to RM202.3 million on stronger performance in its automotive, freight, shipping and warehousing businesses.
The segment's pre-tax loss narrowed to RM29.6 million from RM31.9 million, despite a RM15 million impairment charge on vessels.
Group chief executive officer Charles Brewer said the third-quarter results reflected ongoing efforts to reshape Pos Malaysia.
"Every business segment is growing, led by our courier business, and our nine-month loss before tax is narrowing. We are strengthening the basics of the business, giving us a firmer foundation to build on.
"With the year-end peak ahead, we are ready to build on this momentum. Our focus is clear: keep improving efficiency through disciplined operational focus and, of course, further leveraging digital innovation and artificial intelligence (AI)," he said in a statement.
Pos Malaysia said the domestic parcel delivery market remained highly competitive and faced structural challenges.
The company expects parcel volumes to increase during the year-end peak season, building on market share gains achieved so far.
It will continue to focus on business transformation, digital and AI-driven efficiency, disciplined cost management and regulatory reform.
"The board expects financial performance for financial year 2026 to remain challenging, with the pace of recovery dependent on, among others, the implementation of a sustainable universal service obligation funding framework," it said.

Title: Johor dengue cases surge 159pct, deaths rise to 18
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor recorded 13,641 dengue cases and 18 deaths as of yesterday, marking a 159.4 per cent increase in infections and an 80 per cent rise in fatalities compared with the corresponding period last year.
State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said 275 cases were reported in Epidemiological Week 45, up 3.4 per cent from 266 cases the previous week.
Johor Baru recorded the highest number of cases last week, with 173 or 62.9 per cent of the state total, followed by Kulai with 70 cases (25.5 per cent).
The remaining cases were reported in Kluang and Pontian (seven each), Segamat (six), Kota Tinggi (four), Muar (three), Mersing and Batu Pahat (two each), and Tangkak (one).
Ling said 17 new dengue outbreak localities were reported during the week, comprising 10 in Johor Baru, six in Kulai and one in Kluang.
The cumulative number of outbreak localities reached 1,489 this year, compared with 532 during the corresponding period last year, an increase of 180 per cent.
He said enforcement operations had resulted in 5,338 compounds worth RM2.669 million being issued this year, of which 76.19 per cent had been paid.
However, inspections continued to uncover potential mosquito breeding sites inside and outside homes, indicating that residents were still not doing enough to eliminate stagnant water.
Ling called on the public to spend at least 10 minutes checking and eliminating potential Aedes breeding grounds at home and workplaces, including containers that could collect stagnant water.
Residents were also advised to cover water storage containers, remove stagnant water and scrub containers to eliminate mosquito larvae.
Schools were encouraged to organise regular clean-up activities, while school bus operators and drivers were advised to use aerosol sprays inside buses before morning and afternoon student journeys.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Exsim Hospitality proposed RM226mil acquisition of tower F at Empire City
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Exsim Hospitality Bhd, through its subsidiary Blossom Hectares Sdn Bhd, has entered into a call option agreement with Iconic Insight Sdn Bhd to facilitate the proposed acquisition of Tower F at Empire City, Damansara Perdana for RM226 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the proposed purchase consideration represents a discount of RM2 million, or approximately 0.877 per cent, to the building's market value of RM228 million.
Tower F is currently under construction and is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.
The purchase consideration will be fully settled in cash and funded through a combination of bank borrowings and internally generated funds.
Exsim Hospitality said the proposed acquisition aligns with its strategy to expand its directly owned hospitality assets under its own-and-operate business through acquisitions in locations with attractive long-term growth and capital appreciation potential.
On completion, Tower F will be included in the group's own-and-operate business portfolio and is expected to contribute recurring income once operations commence.
The company said the proposed acquisition is not expected to materially alter the group's business risk profile, as it is already involved in the hospitality sector.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Works Ministry gets half of RM5bil–RM6bil requested for road maintenance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Works Ministry received only about half of the RM5 billion to RM6 billion it sought for road maintenance, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan told the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the ministry received RM2.68 billion in 2026, while RM2.59 billion was approved for 2027.
Ahmad said the shortfall was among the reasons road maintenance and resurfacing works nationwide could not be carried out to the extent required.
"When honourable members raise the issue of roads that have not been fully paved or need resurfacing, one of the causes is budget constraints.
"It is not that the ministry did not apply. We applied for between RM5 billion and RM6 billion, but received only about RM2.5 billion, which is half of what is needed," he said.
He was winding up for the Works Ministry during the committee-stage debate on its 2027 Budget allocation.
Ahmad said the Finance Ministry and the Economy Ministry should take note of the shortfall to ensure actual maintenance needs were considered when allocations were drawn up.
"I do not intend to blame any party, but it is important for the Finance and Economy ministries to look at the overall budget needs that are very important to the people, especially road maintenance," he said.
He said although the Works Ministry received the highest development allocation among the 28 ministries, the amount was still insufficient to meet all its needs, particularly road maintenance.
Ahmad said the ministry's road maintenance allocation was RM1.6 billion in 2021, RM1.17 billion in 2022, RM1.71 billion in 2023, RM2.39 billion in 2024, RM2.99 billion in 2025 and RM2.68 billion in 2026.
On alternative approaches to road paving, he said the ministry, through the Public Works Department's Centre of Excellence for Engineering and Technology (CREaTE), was researching more durable paving materials.
These included mixtures using crumb rubber, rubber from gloves and discarded plastic.
However, he said the cost of using such materials remained higher than conventional paving because they were not yet widely used.
"Still, when we want to implement it, the cost of the materials is rather higher than ordinary paving. That is another constraint.
"However, if the allocation is sufficient, all these matters can be resolved," he said.

Title: Xpeng plans to reorganise distribution network in Malaysia: Bermaz Auto
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bermaz Auto Bhd announced that Xpeng Inc, China, the marque owner and principal manufacturer of Xpeng vehicles, plans to reorganise its Xpeng distribution network in Malaysia.
Its 85 per cent-owned subsidiary, Bermaz Xpeng Sdn Bhd (BXpeng), has ceased its Xpeng operations with effect from today.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the car distributor said both parties concerned are currently finalising the terms to terminate the Xpeng agreements and other ancillary agreements.
"The company will make an announcement in due course once the separation agreement is signed.
"During this period, BXpeng will continue to work with the parties concerned to ensure a smooth transition," it said.
The cessation of BXpeng as the distributor of Xpeng vehicles in Malaysia is not expected to have any material financial or operational impact on the Bermaz group for the current financial year, it added.
Recently, BXpeng had entered into a distributor and a warranty claim agreement with Xpeng Inc  pertaining to the distribution, provision of after-sales services and sale of spare parts for Xpeng vehicles in Malaysia. The agreements are due to expire in March 2027.

Title: Could earlier intervention have saved Orang Asli man who died in custody?
Article:
KUANTAN: The inquest into the death of an Orang Asli man in police custody at Pekan police headquarters two years ago began today, with a lawyer representing his family questioning whether he could have been saved through immediate intervention.
Counsel Datuk Bob Arumugam, who is holding a watching brief for the family, told the Coroner's Court that there was a 24-minute gap between the time Norazman Me was seen attempting to hang himself using his lock-up attire at 1.46am on May 4, 2024, and when the officer on duty realised what had happened at 2.10am.
He said closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed that the incident went unnoticed for 24 minutes, raising questions about whether anyone was monitoring the surveillance cameras at the time.
"From the CCTV image, there was a 24-minute gap during which nobody appeared to be monitoring the footage. Could he have been brought down immediately if the incident had been noticed earlier? He might still have been alive," he said during cross-examination.
Earlier, Pekan police chief Superintendent Mohd Zaidi Mat Zin, the first witness to testify, explained 20 CCTV screenshots captured at the police headquarters, including footage of the lock-up area and the cell where Norazman was found.
Deputy public prosecutor Khamisah Ismail, who is conducting the inquest, had asked Zaidi to identify the individuals shown in the images and explain the sequence of events, including the timestamps leading up to the final image showing Norazman's body being taken out of the lock-up around 7am.
On safety measures introduced after the incident, Zaidi said officers on duty, who were previously required to inspect the lock-up once an hour, had been instructed to conduct rounds every 30 minutes.
"We no longer keep an accused person alone in a cell. Instead, we place two people in each cell," he said.
Norazman's family had
sought answers
after being informed that the 25-year-old father of one was found dead in his cell at Pekan police headquarters on May 4, 2024.
He was arrested on suspicion of vehicle theft on May 1 and remanded until May 6 after testing positive for morphine.
A post-mortem conducted at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital here recorded the cause of death as hanging.
On Oct 24, 2024, Bukit Aman's Integrity and Standards Compliance Department
said it would hand over the investigation findings into Norazman's death to the coroner.
The inquest will continue on Jan 27 and 28 next year before Coroner Sazlina Safie.
Also present in court today were Norazman's parents, Me Kingking, 60, and Noriah Hitam, 53, and one of his siblings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lac Med bags RM28mil contract to provide diagnostic imaging solution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lac Med Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary Lac Medical Supplies Sdn Bhd has bagged a RM28.10 million contract for the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of multiple modalities in radiology and women's imaging for a private hospital in the northern region.
The integrated medical technology solutions provider said the works are expected to be completed by Aug 1, 2027, subject to an extension of time as provided under the contract's conditions.
The warranty period is 24 months for each item of equipment starting from the date of the customer's written acceptance of successful installation, testing and commissioning, it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today.
Lac Med said the contract is expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings in the financial year ending Dec 31, 2027, and net assets throughout the tenure of the contract.
Meanwhile, in a press statement, Lac Med group chief executive officer Liew Yoon Poh said this contract marks the beginning of more things to come with the new client, as it help the hospital's clinical teams use these technologies with confidence.
"As a multi-solutions partner, we have the breadth of products and technical expertise to introduce further solutions as our new client grows in scale and scope of its healthcare services," he said.
Including the latest contract, Lac Med's order book has strengthened to RM288.1 million as at Nov 15, 2026, up from RM230.5 million as at Sept 30, 2026, and providing earnings visibility for the next five years.

Title: Ahmad Maslan withdraws 'kencing' remark from pantun after Dewan Rakyat spat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan was forced to withdraw the word "kencing" from a pantun he recited in the Dewan Rakyat today after RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) objected, saying it was a jibe at Pakatan Harapan (PH) members of parliament.
Ahmad was responding to Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu), who asked whether promises to abolish tolls had been made merely to win elections, while winding up the Works Ministry's 2027 Budget allocation debate at the committee stage.
"Yes, there are many more promises not fulfilled. I have a pantun about tolls. Would you like to hear it?" he said.
"If you go fishing, do not forget to bring bait. If you don't want to be conned (kena kencing), support Barisan and Perikatan."
Rayer stood up to ask whether Ahmad was responding as a deputy minister in the unity government or as an Umno leader.
"We cannot just sit here and listen to criticism like this. Do not insult us in the House," he said.
"You are here as a deputy minister. Answer as a deputy minister of the Unity Government. Don't embarrass yourself."
Deputy Dewan Rakyat Speaker Datuk Dr Ramli Mohd Nor said the debate was getting out of hand.
Rayer then invoked the Standing Orders, arguing that Ahmad should not make remarks that took jabs at PH MPs.
"He should not make statements here that jibe at us, as if he is colluding with the other side.
"I ask him to withdraw the word 'kencing'. Apologise to the PH MPs here. It was an impolite statement," he said.
Tempers flared when Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) interjected, claiming that Rayer's objection also appeared to insult the unity government. Rayer responded loudly, telling him not to interrupt.
Ahmad said he might have got carried away with the pantun but insisted that he had not mentioned PH. Ramli then ruled on the use of the word.
"My ruling on the word 'kencing', the word has nothing to do with anyone as such, but in this context it is unparliamentary," he said.
Ahmad continued speaking without explicitly withdrawing the word. When Rayer asked Ramli to make him do so, Ahmad asked whether it was only that particular word that was objectionable.
Ramli said the intention behind the word was what mattered.
"Mr Speaker says withdraw the word 'kencing'. Okay. I withdraw," Ahmad said.
The exchange followed Ahmad's earlier remarks on calls by MPs to abolish tolls during the debate on the Works Ministry's 2027 Budget allocation.
"We have not promised to abolish tolls. We made no promises. So whoever made the promises must answer," he said.
He said abolishing tolls would require an estimated RM400 billion to take over all 34 toll highways, which are operated under 28 concessions.
"Does the government have RM400 billion to take over all 34 toll highways? I ask. RM400 billion is about a year's budget, you know," he said.

Title: Bursa Malaysia snaps five-day losing streak on bargain hunting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia snapped a five-day losing streak, ending higher on Monday, supported by bargain hunting in selected blue-chip counters, said an analyst.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 5.44 points or 0.34 per cent to 1,588.03 from Friday's close of 1,582.59.
The benchmark index opened 6.69 points lower at 1,575.90 and moved between 1,572.55 and 1,593.02 during the trading session.
However, market breadth remained negative with losers thumping gainers 673 to 375, while 522 counters were unchanged, 1,214 untraded and 16 suspended.
Turnover declined to 2.76 billion units valued at RM2.33 billion from Friday's 2.84 billion units valued at RM2.36 billion.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the FBM KLCI's position near oversold territory, coupled with increasingly attractive valuations, could encourage further bargain hunting, particularly in fundamentally sound blue-chip stocks offering sustainable dividends.
"Investors will also monitor Malaysia's upcoming economic releases, the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes and Nvidia Corp's earnings for fresh direction.
"While external uncertainties could prolong market volatility, we anticipate the FBM KLCI to consolidate within 1,580-1,600 this week, with selective accumulation likely to provide support at lower levels," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Berjaya Research Sdn Bhd head of research Kenneth Leong said the local bourse has formed a bullish candlestick pattern, positioning it for a potential technical rebound.
"The immediate resistance levels are pegged at 1,600 to 1,616 points, while support levels are seen at 1,576 and 1,560 points," he said.
Among heavyweight stocks, Malayan Banking Bhd rose four sen to RM9.98, while Public Bank Bhd added one sen to RM4.55. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd climbed eight sen to RM7.16, while IHH Healthcare Bhd gained three sen to RM7.96. However, Tenaga Nasional Bhd decreased two sen to RM12.74.
In active trade, GIIB Holdings Bhd added five sen to 18 sen, while Ni Hsin Group Bhd was 2.5 sen up at 12.5 sen and Sime Darby Bhd gained eight sen to RM2.56. However, MMAG Holdings Bhd lost half a sen to 2.5 sen and Zetrix AI Bhd was unchanged at six sen.
Among the top gainers, Nestle (M) Bhd surged RM1.42 to RM94.42, while Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd added 40 sen to RM37.60. Mega Fortris bhd improved 37 sen to RM1.61, while Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd went up 32 sen to RM20.10. Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd widened 24 sen to RM21.10.
UMS Integration Limited led the decliners, falling 85 sen to RM6.15. MN Holdings Bhd dipped 21 sen to RM3.36. New Hoong Fatt Holdings Bhd erased 19 sen to RM1.14. Allianz Malaysia Bhd and Solarvest Holdings Bhd slid 18 sen each to RM19.10 and 3.90.

Title: Anwar, Li Qiang reaffirm commitment to deepen Malaysia-China ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and China are committed to expanding bilateral cooperation across various fields to create more opportunities that benefit both countries, says Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The prime minister said this was reaffirmed during his meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila.
"In my meeting with Premier Li Qiang, I expressed my appreciation for the warm welcome and hospitality extended during my recent visit to Hangzhou and Shanghai, which reflected the close friendship between Malaysia and China.
"I also conveyed my appreciation for the progress made in bilateral cooperation across various fields, as well as our shared commitment to further expand areas of cooperation that would benefit both countries," he said in a Facebook post.
Earlier, Anwar attended the 29th Asean-China Summit, where he delivered Malaysia's national statement.
On Sept 22, Anwar made a three-day working visit to Hangzhou and Shanghai at the invitation of the Chinese government. It was his fourth visit to China since becoming prime minister in 2022.
Anwar said he also looked forward to Malaysia's participation in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18 and 19, including the Apec CEO Summit to be hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping.
He expressed hope that the meetings would create new opportunities to further strengthen economic cooperation and ties between Malaysia and China.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 27,000 hair dye bottles worth RM1.08mil seized over fake halal logos [WATCH]
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR: Enforcement officers seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye worth RM1.08 million after uncovering the misuse of Malaysian halal logos.
Penang Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director S. Jegan said the raid on a rented warehouse here followed three weeks of intelligence gathering and public complaints.
Two warehouse workers in their 30s, a woman and a Chinese national, were detained to assist in investigations.
Jegan said the company had imported the hair dye from China and sold it exclusively through social media and e-commerce platforms, including TikTok, Shopee and Lazada.
"In six months of operations, they managed to sell nearly 600,000 units at RM40 per box.
[[nid:1579193]]
"This is a major concern because hair dye is widely used, including by the elderly. It was a 'hot killer item' in the warehouse," he told reporters at the scene.
Jegan said investigations found that the product packaging displayed a generic halal logo without a valid serial number, while promotional videos featured influential affiliates and even religious figures displaying a Malaysian halal certificate belonging to another company.
"It is a clear-cut offence as the product does not have valid Malaysian halal certification from the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) or any State Islamic Religious Council," he added.
The case is being investigated under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 (Act 730).
Upon conviction, individuals face a fine of up to RM1 million, a jail term of up to three years or both, while companies face a fine of up to RM5 million.
Jegan advised consumers to verify halal claims directly through the Jakim portal before purchasing products online, rather than relying solely on social media affiliates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gamuda secures RM2.6bil MRT construction contract in Taiwan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd, through an 80:20 joint venture (JV) with Taiwan-based Feng Shun Construction Co Ltd, has secured a contract worth NT$21.02 billion (approximately RM2.61 billion) to undertake the design and construction of the Keelung Underground Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) project in Taiwan.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the engineering and construction company said the Department of Rapid Transit Systems, New Taipei City Government awarded the contract on Nov 16, 2026.
"The project comprises 2.4 km of underground works located across Nangang District (Taipei City) to Xizhi District (New Taipei City), including two underground stations.
"It is expected to be completed within 7.4 years," the company said.
It said the project incorporates environmental, social and governance principles through the use of eco-friendly materials, energy-efficient systems and sustainable construction practices.
'The project is expected to contribute positively to its revenue and earnings for the financial year ending July 31, 2027, until its completion," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EcoWorld, Permodalan Darul Ta'zim explore renewable energy, water supply for Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) has signed an agreement with Permodalan Darul Ta'zim Sdn Bhd (PDT) to explore supplying renewable electricity and reclaimed water to data centres and industrial parks in Johor.
Under the agreement, PDT will facilitate the supply of green utilities through PDT Energy Sdn Bhd and Johor Special Water Sdn Bhd (JSW) to EcoWorld's industrial and data centre customers, subject to pricing and other commercial terms to be finalised.
EcoWorld will promote these utilities to its network of green consumers and provide the utility suppliers with information on customers' anticipated consumption, demand forecasts and timelines, subject to their consent where required.
EcoWorld said its Quantum and Eco Business Parks have a growing network of eligible green energy consumers and other potential customers.
PDT, the Johor government's strategic investment arm, is responsible for implementing the Johor Green Development Policy 2030 and leading efforts to supply green utilities in the state.
Through PDT Energy and its joint venture partners, PDT plans to supply renewable electricity and renewable energy certificates to eligible consumers under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme and other potential customers.
JSW, meanwhile, holds exclusive rights to supply raw water, treated effluent, reclaimed water and alternative water for industrial use in Johor.
"By seamlessly connecting the supply dynamics of green utilities with clear projections of actual demand, the collaboration agreement supports the state's aims to drive green investments and technology adoption while encouraging industries to improve energy efficiency and optimising the use of water resources.
"Together, these efforts will help sustain Johor's momentum in high value economic growth, while ensuring EcoWorld's industrial projects continue to be supported by reliable, efficient and sustainable utilities," EcoWorld said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen mistaken for mouse deer, shot with homemade gun
Article:
RANAU: A 15-year-old girl was seriously injured after being shot with a homemade firearm, known locally as a 'bakakuk', after being mistaken for a mouse deer while searching for frogs near a river in Kampung Tinanom here on Saturday night.
The incident occurred around 10pm, leaving the victim with about 13 injuries to several parts of her body, including her neck, chest, shoulders, hands and right knee.
Ranau police chief Superintendent Mursalin Mahmud said police had arrested a 40-year-old man, who is related to the victim, to assist in investigations.
He said the suspect, a farmer, was detained by a team from the Ranau district Criminal Investigation Division at 1.30pm yesterday.
"Preliminary investigations found that the suspect had gone hunting with a homemade firearm, moving along the Sungai Keliu area.
"When he was there, he spotted a light which he mistook for the eyes of a mouse deer and fired a shot.
"However, he later heard cries of pain before discovering that the person he had shot was the girl," he said when contacted today.
Mursalin said the victim had gone to the river with a family member and another man to catch fish and look for frogs before the incident.
The injured girl was taken back to the village before receiving emergency treatment at Paginatan Health Clinic.
"She was initially conscious but experienced breathing difficulties before being transferred to Ranau Hospital for further treatment.
"Examinations found that she had sustained multiple injuries believed to have been caused by the gunshot, including a fracture to her left wrist. She was also placed in an induced coma," he said.
The victim was transferred to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu yesterday afternoon for further examinations and surgery.
Mursalin said investigations also found that the suspect was believed to have discarded the firearm in the forest after the incident.
"The firearm has yet to be recovered, and efforts to locate it are ongoing with the assistance of the forensic team and the D10 division of the Sabah police contingent headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department.
"The case is being investigated under Sections 37 and 8(a) of the Arms Act 1960, while an application for a remand order has been made against the suspect to assist in further investigations," he said.

Title: Singapore warns of 3-hour waits at checkpoints during school holidays
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Motorists travelling between Johor and Singapore have been warned to expect heavy traffic at the Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints during the year-end school holidays.
Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said congestion is expected from Nov 20 to Jan 3, 2027, with immigration clearance potentially taking up to three hours during peak periods.
The warning coincides with Malaysia's year-end school holidays, which run from Dec 5 to Dec 31 for Johor and other Group B states, including Selangor, Penang and Perak.
ICA said more than two million travellers crossed the land checkpoints during the Deepavali long weekend from Nov 6 to Nov 9, peaking at more than 553,000 crossings on Nov 6.
During that period, motorists departing Singapore at peak hours faced waits of up to three hours due to traffic tailbacks from Malaysia.
ICA also warned travellers against presenting incorrect passports or QR codes, noting such cases rose from 46 in July to 74 in September.
Those with incorrect documents or QR codes will be referred for further checks and barred from departing Singapore until valid documents are produced.
To speed up clearance, ICA urged travellers to use QR codes generated via the MyICA mobile application, which has boosted peak departure throughput by more than 35 per cent.
This improvement equals an additional 7,600 travellers per hour compared with pre-Covid-19 levels in 2019.
Motorists were reminded to maintain lane discipline, as queue-cutters will be ordered to make a U-turn and rejoin the queue from the back.
During the Deepavali enforcement operation, 11 departing motorists were caught committing traffic offences at Woodlands Checkpoint.
Six vehicles were ordered to make U-turns, while five drivers of foreign-registered vehicles were banned from entering Singapore for offences including crossing double white lines and queue-cutting.
ICA reminded travellers to ensure their passports have at least six months' validity, while foreign-registered vehicle owners must have valid Vehicle Entry Permits (VEPs), Autopass cards and insurance.
Since Nov 2, foreign-registered vehicles with unpaid
traffic
, parking or vehicular emissions fines cannot apply for or renew their VEPs and will be denied entry into Singapore.
Travellers were advised to avoid early morning and evening peak hours and check traffic conditions before setting off.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Laos to deepen cooperation in energy, infrastructure, trade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Laos have agreed to strengthen bilateral economic and trade cooperation, particularly in renewable energy, infrastructure, transportation and logistics, as the two countries mark 60 years of diplomatic relations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed during his meeting with his Laotian counterpart, Saleumxay Kommasith, on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila, the Philippines.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the meeting also served as a platform to strengthen bilateral ties, while allowing him to congratulate Saleumxay on his appointment as Laos' Prime Minister last month.
On bilateral trade, Anwar said total trade between Malaysia and Laos rose 28.7 per cent to US$55.9 million (RM228.5 million) in the January-August period last year.
He said both countries also agreed to intensify cooperation through the 4th Joint Commission for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) Meeting, scheduled to be held in Vientiane in 2027, while finalising partnerships in higher education and tourism.
The 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits are being held from Nov 15 to 17 under the Philippines' chairmanship.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: French actor Gerard Depardieu withdraws sexual assault appeal, apologises to victims
Article:
PARIS: French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against a 2025 conviction for sexual assault, accepting his guilt and apologising to his victims.
In a statement, Depardieu said he had often used "vulgar, sexually suggestive humour" on set and now realised "there is a line between cheekiness and offence."
He said he offered "his deepest and most sincere apologies to all those who may have suffered as a result", adding that he had chosen to pull his appeal as he had "come to realise that I belonged to a world that no longer exists."
Depardieu – a towering figure in French cinema, who starred in more than 200 films over five decades, including Green Card, The Last Metro and Cyrano de Bergerac – was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on a film set in May 2025.
He received an 18-month suspended sentence, with the judge saying he appeared not to have grasped the "traumatic" impact of his behaviour.
Depardieu still faces the prospect of a trial for allegedly raping actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He denies guilt.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man who robbed motorist, KK Mart workers at knifepoint jailed 10 years, caned
Article:
TELUK INTAN: A man who robbed a motorist of RM4,030 at knifepoint and later stole gold jewellery and cash from KK Mart employees in separate incidents has been sentenced to a total of 10 years in jail and four strokes of the rotan.
However, Azizul Azmil Abdul Aziz, 26, failed in his bid to have the five-year jail term for the first robbery run concurrently with the sentence imposed in the second case.
Sessions court judge Norhamizah Shaiffuddin ruled that the sentences must run consecutively as the offences were committed on different dates and involved different victims.
In the first incident, at 4.10am on Jan 29, Azizul and an accomplice, who is still at large, approached a motorist who had stopped at an emergency lay-by along the North-South Expressway at Km366 to rest.
The duo threatened the victim with a knife and demanded money, prompting him to hand over RM4,030 before they fled on a motorcycle.
In the second incident on July 1, Azizul and another accomplice, who is also still at large, robbed two employees at a KK Mart outlet in Slim River.
They took the employees' gold necklaces and earrings before threatening them with a knife and forcing them to open the cash register. They then fled with all the cash inside.
Azizul was sentenced to five years in jail and two strokes of the rotan for each robbery after pleading guilty to both charges under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code.
In his appeal, he sought to have the jail terms run concurrently, citing his early guilty pleas, cooperation with police, the fact that his accomplices remained at large and that nobody was injured.
The court was also told that he was unemployed, unmarried and financially supported by his 53-year-old mother, who works as a People's Volunteer Corps member.
However, Norhamizah said public interest must take precedence over the accused's personal interests, noting that armed robberies caused significant trauma to victims.
"Such gang robberies occur far too frequently and cause considerable trauma to victims, particularly when deadly weapons are used, further heightening their fear.
"The court also took into account that none of the victims had recovered their stolen cash or jewellery," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jordan bans Telegram app over 'radicalisation' claims
Article:
AMMAN: Jordan announced a ban on the Telegram messaging app on Monday, citing concerns that it was being used to spread extremism, weeks after a deadly attack on a church.
"We announce the blocking of the Telegram app in Jordan, in the framework of efforts aiming to bolster digital security and protext users," the Jordanian security directorate said.
It said the move came "in the context of the commitment to protecting society and countering any uses that could contribute to and facilitate committing cyber crimes, threats, blackmail or spreading illegal content."
It also said it sought to counter "attempt to spread radicalisation and extremism which affects national security."
The ban comes after the Oct 23 attack on a church in the southern Karak governorate that killed nine people and wounded dozens of others.
On Sunday, a court sentenced three men to death by hanging over the attack. Authorities described them as followers of a hardline Islamist ideology.
Jordan also banned TikTok in December 2022, citing the dissemination of videos authorities described as "inciting killing and chaos."
That ban followed protests over rising fuel costs, during which violence erupted, with one security officer killed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLSCAH land premium cut unreasonable, potentially controversial, says academic
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decision to reduce the land premium for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) from an initial estimate of RM4.67 million to RM1,000 has been described as unreasonable and potentially controversial.
National Council of Professors senior fellow Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Teo Kok Seong said the vast difference between the two figures was difficult to justify, particularly as the decision was made shortly after a change in leadership overseeing the portfolio.
"The initial premium of millions of ringgit must have been based on concrete grounds and reasons," he said in a statement today.
Teo said the earlier premium estimate must have had a basis, despite KLSCAH being gazetted as a heritage site in 2007.
He said the proposal to reduce land premiums for several other heritage sites in Kuala Lumpur appeared to be an attempt to ease the backlash over the KLSCAH decision.
The decision to impose a nominal RM1,000 premium for the renewal of KLSCAH's land lease for 99 years was announced by Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh at the association's 103rd anniversary dinner on Nov 14.
Earlier, the Federal Territories Land Committee had approved the surrender and re-alienation of the land for institutional use on Sept 14.
Describing the reduction as insensitive, he warned that disputes over the decision could affect social harmony.
He also questioned the use of languages other than Bahasa Melayu at the announcement ceremony, saying the national language should have been given priority as the announcement involved an official government decision.
"The ceremony should have been conducted using the official language, but Bahasa Melayu was not given priority," said Teo.
He said the recurring issue, despite repeated reminders, should be addressed by government agencies.
Earlier, Yeoh said the reduction followed the conversion of
KLSCAH's land status
from commercial to institutional use, meaning it no longer carried commercial value and could not be developed for condominiums or shopping malls.
She said KLSCAH, which was gazetted as a heritage building in early 2007, had eight years remaining on its lease when it applied for the reduction.
The non-profit organisation had appealed based on its long history and heritage status, she added.
"On that basis, the valuation committee agreed to reduce the lease premium to RM1,000 since the land status has been restricted to institutional use only," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's resilient economy to support real estate market in 2027 – Juwai IQI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's resilient economic outlook is expected to continue supporting its real estate market as it heads into 2027, according to international real estate technology group Juwai IQI.
Its co-founder and group chief executive officer, Kashif Ansari, said Malaysia was the only one among nine Asian economies to record a decline in food inflation from an already low level, while also benefiting from low headline inflation, steady economic growth and rising per capita income.
He said the country's resilient real estate market is due to several factors, including government policies, natural resources and an innovative population.
"When you look at the economic data, the clearest sign is this. Malaysia moved up two spots among the nine (economies), measured by gross domestic product (GDP) in US dollars.
"In 2025, Malaysia was the sixth-largest economy of the nine, but this year it looks like it has jumped to fourth-largest, passing two regional peers on the way, even though it has the second-smallest population of the nine, after Sri Lanka, with 34.2 million people," he said in a statement today.
Kashif said Malaysia's resilient economy had helped keep the housing market on firm ground, with 187,320 property transactions worth RM105.12 billion recorded in the first half of 2026.
He said Johor recorded the highest house price growth among the major states at 3.6 per cent, followed by Kuala Lumpur at 2.7 per cent, while high-rise property prices rose 0.9 per cent, faster than a year earlier.
"The Malaysian House Price Index rose 0.9 per cent year on year in the second quarter, to 234.7 points, and the average house price nationwide is now RM506,317.
"Families who are saving to buy a home are happy when prices remain steady and within reach. With inflation under control, interest rates have also remained stable," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI cheating sparks alarm ahead of South Korea's college exam
Article:
A South Korean exam cheat who confessed to using AI to post near-perfect accountancy test scores has sent teachers and officials scrambling to prevent similar misconduct ahead of this week's crucial college entrance exam.
Known as the Suneung, the intense once-a-year exam will bring much of South Korea to a standstill on Thursday, with flights temporarily halted during the English listening section and stock trading delayed by an hour.
The trickster's admission on Sunday to using a miniature camera and smartphone in two national tax tests earlier this year has "caused panic among teachers", said Kim Seung-ho, a high school educator in the central city of Cheongju.
"Each testing centre is assigned six to seven metal detectors, but not enough for every classroom," he told AFP, adding "the problem is we don't know if they can detect miniature cameras or nano-scale earphones."
More than half a million students are set to sit the gruelling nine-hour test this year in highly competitive South Korea, where getting into a top university is seen as a ticket not only to well-paid jobs but also to better marriage prospects.
Song Ji-eun, who will take the test, told AFP that she would struggle to concentrate "if supervisors keep checking my glasses" for tiny cameras.
"There's a saying that even a slight breeze can affect your focus, your score and even your entire life," the 18-year-old said.
The cheating revelation prompted South Korea's presidential office to announce plans to deploy thermal cameras at exam centres, though it was unclear whether they would be installed at all 1,312 testing sites.
Education officials were also considering suspending public Wi-Fi hotspots near college entrance exam sites.
"We are reviewing all measures, including suspending public Wi-Fi networks," an education ministry official told AFP, adding that an announcement would be made before the exam takes place.
According to local media reports, the government has also been discussing cutting off 5G and LTE mobile data around exam sites and activating signal-jamming devices.
"As devices themselves have become more advanced, including those that can be attached to the body, it is not easy to detect 100 percent of cheating without completely blocking communications," Vice Education Minister Choi Eun-ok said.
However, experts say it would be technically impossible as it would disrupt communication in surrounding residential areas and block emergency calls.
Asked whether signal-blocking measures could be introduced at examination centres, Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin said his office was consulting with the science ministry "to see whether it would be possible, even for part of the examination."
The minister rejected calls for the exam to be rescheduled, saying it "could cause even greater confusion."
The test cheat's video confession, which was posted on his lawyer's YouTube channel, came after questions were raised about his performance.
He ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam, answering all but one of 160 questions correctly in the first round, a feat many tax accountants had deemed nearly impossible.
His confession has also fuelled suspicions that AI-assisted deception may have already taken place in other high-stakes exams, including law school admissions and university transfer tests.
Lee Jin-woo, who earned a perfect score on a law school admission test in July and has since gained celebrity-like status, has faced scrutiny over his results, prompting him to announce plans to livestream himself solving the Korean language section of the Suneung on Thursday to prove his abilities.
It comes as officials plan to review all cases involving suspected cheating in state-administered professional licensing exams.
But teacher Kim said the response had come too late.
"We had two mock college admission exams in June and September, when we could have tested our readiness to prevent AI-assisted cheating," he said.
"But we did nothing in terms of preventive training, wasting our opportunities to prepare for the real Suneung."
Experts warn that any breach of the college admission test could have serious repercussions, threatening public confidence in an exam seen as a cornerstone of meritocracy in the country.
"Suneung is a symbol of fairness in South Korea, where students compete on equal terms regardless of their background or circumstances," said Kim Seong-sheen, a professor at Hanyang University's Institute for Creative Convergence Education.
"If AI devices can compromise this exam, the issue goes far beyond a single act of cheating. It would mean undermining public trust in the entire examination system."
* The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN MPs demand Anwar address Rafizi's 'corporate mafia' claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional members of parliament have called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to address Parti Bersama Malaysia president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli's "corporate mafia" claims in the Dewan Rakyat.
They also want answers on six other allegations raised by Rafizi during the Melaka election campaign, including a RM9.5 million payment to a minister and potential losses of RM472 million in public funds involving Zetrix AI.
In a statement read by Kinabatangan MP Mohd Kurniawan Naim Moktar at Parliament today, the MPs said the claims warranted answers despite Bersama failing to win any of the 16 seats it contested.
They backed the special task force led by the attorney-general and called for its findings to be made public, subject to the law.
They also urged police to complete their investigation into the alleged RM9.5 million payment to Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, who has denied the claim.
The MPs also sought answers on alleged interference in NexG Bhd, government-linked investment in Zetrix AI, the RM1.05 billion National Integrated Immigration System project, RM314 million in Road Transport Department revenue arrears and former MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki's shareholdings.
"Any allegation that has basis must be investigated independently and professionally without political interference. If there is evidence of wrongdoing, legal action must be taken regardless of the position of the individuals involved," the statement read.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MRL plans Malaysia's first tokenised infrastructure sukuk
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) plans to issue Malaysia's first tokenised government-guaranteed infrastructure sukuk under its RM19.05 billion sukuk programme to finance the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project.
The proposed issuance, which is subject to regulatory approval, will see CIMB Investment Bank Bhd serve as the sole lead arranger.
If implemented, MRL will become the first entity under Minister of Finance Incorporated and the first government-guaranteed infrastructure sukuk issuer in Malaysia to undertake a tokenised issuance.
MRL said the initiative would explore the use of digital financial infrastructure to support the ECRL's financing needs, potentially enabling faster settlement, better liquidity management, greater transparency and more efficient fund transfers.
It is also expected to broaden investment opportunities in Malaysia's digital capital markets by introducing government-guaranteed sukuk into the growing tokenised investment ecosystem.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said Malaysia's established position in Islamic finance provided a strong foundation for adopting new financial technologies while maintaining governance, transparency and investor protection.
"The ECRL is a strategic national infrastructure project that is expected to enhance connectivity between the East Coast and the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia, facilitate the movement of people and goods, stimulate economic activity and support more balanced regional development.
"Initiatives such as this demonstrate how strategic national projects can also contribute to the continued development of Malaysia's capital markets while supporting long-term infrastructure financing needs," he said.
MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said the collaboration with CIMB would allow the company to explore new financing approaches for the national rail project.
He said tokenisation could improve settlement processes, liquidity management and transparency in the ECRL's financing arrangements.
"The ECRL is on track for commercial operations beginning Dec 12, 2026, to serve as a green mode of transportation for both passengers and freight along its electrified rail network that links the East Coast states with the Klang Valley," he said.
CIMB Group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin said the collaboration built on the bank's experience in pioneering tokenised sukuk issuances with Khazanah Nasional Bhd.
He said the proposed issuance would make MRL Malaysia's first non-financial corporate issuer of tokenised sukuk, marking another milestone in the development of the country's digital capital markets.
The initiative also aims to demonstrate how emerging financial technologies can support strategic national infrastructure financing while maintaining the regulatory, governance and Shariah standards of Malaysia's Islamic capital market.
The signing of a letter of intent between MRL and CIMB was witnessed by Amir Hamzah and Chief Secretary to the Government and MRL chairman Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor identifies 56 flood hotspots ahead of Northeast Monsoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Rainfall exceeding 100 millimetres within just over two hours could trigger flash floods in Kampung Melayu Subang and surrounding areas if rivers and local drainage systems are unable to cope with the volume of water.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the two main rivers contributing to overflow in the area were Sungai Damansara and Sungai Buluh.
“In areas currently at risk of flooding, the overflowing water comes from Sungai Damansara and Sungai Buluh. In Kampung Melayu Subang, flooding is also influenced by overflow from the local drainage system,” he told Bernama today.
He said the overflow could also affect several other areas, including Shah Alam, Puncak Alam, Paya Jaras and Kampung Kubu Gajah, before flowing towards Kampung Parit Mahang, Ijok, Cerakah and Kampung Bukit Kuching, eventually reaching Kuala Selangor.
In preparation for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), Selangor JBPM has identified 56 flood hotspots and 232 flood-prone areas statewide.
Klang has the highest number of flood hotspots, with 13, followed by Petaling (11), Gombak (10), Hulu Langat (nine), Kuala Selangor (six), Sepang (three), and Kuala Langat and Hulu Selangor with two each. No flood hotspots have been recorded in Sabak Bernam.
Hulu Langat has the highest number of flood-prone areas at 37, followed by Klang (33), Sepang (32), Kuala Selangor and Gombak (29 each), Petaling (27), Kuala Langat (22), Hulu Selangor (12) and Sabak Bernam (11).
Ashrul Riezal said the department had 1,603 firefighters and 1,251 volunteer members  on standby, supported by 71 rescue boats, 12 operational lorries and 68 four-wheel-drive vehicles to deal with possible flooding during the monsoon.
Kampung Melayu Subang is among the areas in Selangor prone to recurring floods. Heavy rain earlier this month caused several homes there to be inundated.
Following the incident, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Nov 3 directed that the implementation of the nearly RM700 million Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara Flood Mitigation Projects be expedited. — Bernama

Title: Pasir Gudang MP hands over phone as police probe viral poem
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Pasir Gudang Member of Parliament Hassan Abdul Karim gave his statement at Bukit Aman today regarding his poem titled
Patik Tak Rela
which went viral on social media.
He arrived at the police headquarters at 2:50 pm to give his statement to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT), with the recording of his statement conducted by the investigating officer starting at 3:00 pm.
“I gave my full cooperation and answered nearly 20 questions posed throughout the investigation session,” he said when met by reporters after finishing his statement.
He informed that his mobile phone was also handed over to the police to assist with further investigations.
However, Hassan declined to comment on the meaning of the poem, expressing concern that his remarks might contradict the official statement already recorded.
“The poem has already gone viral, so it is up to the public to make their own interpretations. I cannot explain it here,” he said.
It is understood that the investigation is being conducted under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. — Bernama

Title: Two held as KPDN confiscates 27,000 hair dye products bearing suspected unauthorised halal logo
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 16 — The Penang branch of the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye products worth RM1.08 million suspected of misusing the Malaysian halal logo without a valid Malaysian Halal Certification (SPHM) in a raid on a warehouse in Kampung Selamat here today.
Penang KPDN director S. Jegan said the seizure was made during an inspection conducted at about 1pm following complaints and three weeks of intelligence gathering by the ministry's enforcement officers.
"In the raid, we seized 27,000 bottles of hair dye products stored in the warehouse and detained two company employees, a local woman and a Chinese national man, both in their 30s, to assist in investigations.
"Preliminary investigations found that the products were suspected of displaying the Malaysian halal logo although the company failed to produce valid halal certification documents to substantiate the use of the logo,” he told a media conference at the warehouse here today.
He said investigations also revealed that the hair dye products were imported from China and stored at a warehouse rented by the company before being marketed online through social media and e-commerce platforms such as TikTok, Shopee and Lazada.
Jegan said the company was believed to have been operating for the past six months, with an estimated 600,000 units of the products sold during that period, each bottle of hair dye retailing at RM40.
He said the company's modus operandi included displaying suspected fake halal certificates in advertisements on social media and e-commerce platforms, as well as engaging popular social media influencers and affiliate agents to convince consumers of the products' halal status.
"Our inspection also found that the halal certificate displayed in their promotional materials actually belonged to another company and not the company marketing the products. The Malaysian halal logo was also displayed on the product packaging despite the company not having a valid SPHM for the products,” he said.
He said the matter was particularly concerning as the hair dye was a personal care product used by various segments of society, including senior citizens, and misuse of the halal logo could mislead consumers and undermine confidence in the integrity of the country's halal certification system.
He said further investigations were underway, including efforts to trace the company owner, and the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 (Act 730).
He advised consumers to verify the halal status of products through the official website of the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM), particularly before making purchases, and not to rely entirely on sellers' claims or affiliate promotions. — Bernama

Title: Dentist fined RM70,000 over use of unregistered staff for dental work
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — A dentist was fined RM70,000 by the Sessions Court here today after being found guilty of two charges of employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner and allowing the person to perform dental procedures at her clinic two years ago.
Judge Noor Ruzilawati Mohd Noor imposed a fine of RM30,000 for the first charge and RM40,000 for the second, with six and seven months’ imprisonment respectively in default of payment.
Dr Tong Soo Huan, 38, was charged with employing an individual who was not registered as a dental practitioner under the Dental Act 2018 at a dental clinic in Jalan SS21/1 here at 12.50 pm on May 6, 2024.
The charge was brought under Section 68 of the Dental Act 2018, which provides for a maximum fine of RM300,000 or imprisonment for up to six years, or both.
She was also charged with allowing an individual who was not registered under the Act to practise dentistry at her clinic on the same date and time, under Section 69(a) of the same Act, which carries the same maximum penalty.
According to the facts of the case, on May 6, 2024, a team of enforcement officers from the Selangor State Health Department conducted an inspection at Dr Tong’s clinic and found a female staff member scanning a patient’s teeth using an iTero Element intraoral scanner.
The inspection found that the staff member was not registered with the Malaysian Dental Council (MDC) as a dental practitioner, while Dr Tong, who was a registered dental practitioner, failed to produce the staff member’s annual practising certificate when requested by the enforcement officers.
Earlier, Health Ministry (MOH) prosecuting officer Dr Haznita Zainal Abidin urged the court to impose substantial fines for both charges in the interest of public safety and patient protection, noting that the offences were of a strict liability nature and involved the integrity of the dental profession.
“The accused not only failed to ensure that a registered dental practitioner was on duty throughout the clinic’s operating hours, but also deliberately instructed and allowed a clinic staff member whose only qualification was the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) to perform dental procedures, namely intraoral scanning using specialised medical device equipment at the accused’s premises.
“An oral scanning procedure using an intraoral scanner (iTero Element) requires a high level of expertise to operate. Based on testimony from the Medical Device Authority, the device can only be operated by qualified medical or dental practitioners,” she said.
Dr Haznita said the sentence should send a strong message and serve as a stern lesson to the accused and the entire dental practitioner community in Malaysia not to take shortcuts to cut costs or disregard the law by delegating clinical duties to staff without professional qualifications.
However, lawyer Rejinder Singh, representing Dr Tong, appealed for a lighter fine, arguing that his client was a first-time offender and had no previous record of offences under the Dental Act 2018.
“The offence committed was a technical violation and did not involve any criminal element, as a patient had come to the clinic for treatment while Dr Tong was out for lunch at the time.
“The accused is aware of her actions and regrets not exercising greater vigilance in supervising the clinic staff. She has pledged to ensure stricter control measures in the future,” the lawyer said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia targets leadership role in green energy through local expertise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia aspires to be more than just a participant in the energy transition landscape, but instead emerge as a leader, technology owner and creator of opportunities in the green energy sector through the development of local expertise, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
The Energy Transition and Water Transformation minister said energy transition was not just an environmental agenda, but also a catalyst for economic growth that could create high-value employment opportunities and enhance the competitiveness of local industries.
Fadillah said this after officiating the Gading Kencana Solar Farm under the Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP), which was developed through a strategic collaboration between local renewable energy company Gading Kencana Sdn Bhd and global semiconductor company Intel.
"We do not merely want to be participants in the energy transition, but emerge as leaders, technology owners and creators of opportunities in the country’s green energy landscape,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fadillah said the 43-megawatt peak (MWp) solar farm demonstrated that the country’s energy transition was no longer just an aspiration, but was becoming a reality.
He said the project also demonstrated the ability of local companies to gain the trust of international investors through a combination of investment, innovation and expertise.
He said the achievement was particularly commendable as it reflected the ability of Bumiputera companies to expand their participation in high-technology industries, develop expertise and compete internationally.
Meanwhile, Intel had entered into a 15-year long-term agreement to purchase 53,000 Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) annually through the collaboration.
He said the commitment reflected international investors’ confidence in the potential and capabilities of Malaysia’s clean energy ecosystem.
"I hope that the success of Gading Kencana, one of the pioneers of Malaysia’s large-scale solar industry for more than two decades, would inspire more local companies to explore new opportunities, master technologies and develop their own capabilities.
"Indeed, energy transition is a shared commitment and responsibility. Our success is measured not only by the amount of energy generated or the value of investments secured, but by the benefits we can deliver to the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Ministry allocates RM2m for adoption centres as part of stray dog management efforts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) has allocated RM3.362 million to strengthen stray dog management nationwide through financial assistance to local authorities, awareness campaigns and the construction of adoption centres.
Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the allocation included a one-off grant of RM902,471 for local authorities to purchase euthanasia medication and equipment to capture stray dogs.
She said the allocation comprised RM58,841 for 28 local authorities in 2021, RM65,630 for 29 in 2022, RM140,000 for 31 in 2025 and RM638,000 for 71 local authorities in 2026.
"…we have also allocated funds for the Stray Animal Management Campaign, which was launched in 2024. A total of RM180,000 was allocated that year, followed by RM130,000 in 2025 and RM150,000 this year, bringing the total to RM460,000,” she said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Her response followed a question from Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) on efforts to improve the sustainable management of stray dogs nationwide and the ministry's provision of financial assistance to local authorities for stray animal control.
KPKT had also provided RM2 million this year for two adoption centres overseen by Johor Bahru City Council and Sandakan Municipal Council, through its Local Government Department (JKT), Aiman Athirah said.
On the approach to managing stray dogs, she said the ministry followed a four-pronged policy known as trap, reclaim, rehome and dispose.
"Since September, the ministry has directed all local authorities to step up enforcement efforts, including conducting checks on dog ownership and licensing in residential areas to ensure owners comply with the dog licensing by-laws in force in their respective jurisdictions,” she said.
She said local authorities nationwide received 45,804 complaints about stray dog disturbances last year, and 24,195 operations resulted in 80,412 stray dogs being caught.
"Of these, some were handed over to the Department of Veterinary Services, while others were reclaimed by their owners or adopted through dog adoption programmes. These figures reflect KPKT's and local authorities' continued commitment to controlling and managing stray dogs,” she said.
She said the ministry acknowledged the proposal to introduce a more comprehensive national framework for managing stray animals, but any move to strengthen existing mechanisms would be undertaken in phases involving multiple agencies.
She added that KPKT welcomed suggestions from non-governmental organisations on improving stray animal management nationwide, particularly through adoption programmes, shelter facilities and public education.
-- BERNAMA
TAGS: Dewan Rakyat, Special Chamber, KPKT, local authorities, stray dogs

Title: PM: Malaysia, Laos to strengthen bilateral cooperation across key sectors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia and Laos have agreed to step up bilateral economic and trade cooperation, particularly in the fields of renewable energy, infrastructure, transportation, and logistics, in conjunction with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed during his meeting with his Laotian counterpart, Saleumxay Kommasith, on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit currently taking place in Manila, the Philippines.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said that in addition to congratulating Saleumxay on his appointment as Prime Minister of Laos last month, the meeting also served as a platform to strengthen bilateral ties.
Touching on bilateral trade, the Prime Minister noted that total trade between Malaysia and Laos for the January to August period last year increased by 28.7 per cent to US$55.9 million (RM229 million).
He said both nations also agreed to intensify cooperation through the organisation of the 4th Joint Commission for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) Meeting in Vientiane in 2027, alongside finalising partnerships in the higher education and tourism sectors.
The 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits are being held from November 15 to 17 under the chairmanship of the Philippines. — Bernama

Title: Suspected migrant smuggling agent arrested after armed confrontation in Pasir Mas
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 16 — Two suspected migrant smuggling agents, or tekong darat, fled after approaching General Operations Force (GOF) personnel with a machete and a sickle, prompting the officers to point their firearms at them before giving chase in Kubang Gadong, Pasir Mas yesterday.
Southeast Brigade GOF commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the incident occurred at about 8 pm during Ops Taring Delta, when a team conducting surveillance in an oil palm plantation spotted a group of individuals behaving suspiciously.
