“One of the men was arrested along with a sickle, while the other escaped. The operation also led to the detention of 12 migrants, comprising eight men and four women aged between 18 and 36, who failed to produce valid travel documents,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Radzi said an inspection of the arrested man’s mobile phone revealed an image of a bank account number under the name of a local woman, believed to have been used by an agent from Thailand to arrange payments.
Preliminary investigations found that the suspect received RM100 for each migrant brought across the Golok River from Thailand before being handed over to transporters around Kampung Bakong.
He said each migrant was believed to have been charged up to RM5,000 to enter Malaysia illegally, with payment required only after securing employment in the country.
The case is being investigated under Section 26A of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM), Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Section 6 of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958. — Bernama

Title: Anwar welcomes progress in Malaysia-China ties, eyes stronger economic links
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Malaysia and China are committed to expanding bilateral cooperation across various fields to create more opportunities that will benefit both countries.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was reaffirmed during his meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit in Manila.
“In my meeting with Premier Li Qiang, I expressed my appreciation for the warm welcome and hospitality extended during my recent visit to Hangzhou and Shanghai, which reflected the close friendship between Malaysia and China.
“I also conveyed my appreciation for the progress made in bilateral cooperation across various fields, as well as our shared commitment to further expand areas of cooperation that would benefit both countries,” he said in a Facebook post.
Earlier, Anwar attended the 29th Asean-China Summit, where he delivered Malaysia’s national statement.
On September 22, Anwar made a three-day working visit to Hangzhou and Shanghai at the invitation of the Chinese government, his fourth visit to the country since becoming Prime Minister in 2022.
Anwar said he also looked forward to Malaysia’s participation in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18 and 19, including the APEC CEO Summit to be hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping.
He expressed hope that the meetings would open up new opportunities to further strengthen economic cooperation and ties between Malaysia and China. — Bernama

Title: Border economic zone study to guide Malaysia-Thailand border development, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 —The government does not plan to create any new economic corridor in the Wang Kelian area, but will strengthen the framework for the Northern Corridor Region (NCER) and the Border Economic Zone (BEZ), which is being finalised, the Economy Ministry said.
Its Deputy Minister Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah said this approach avoids duplicating functions with the Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA), and simultaneously, maximises potential Malaysia-Thailand cross-border trade.
He said the government is currently finalising a study on the BEZ development involving four states - Perlis, Kedah, Perak and Kelantan.
“This study aims to assess and explore development proposals for the border area with a focus on key strategic border gates.
“Additionally, the Thai government is also finalising a similar study in collaboration with the World Bank to assess the potential development of their territory bordering Malaysia,” he said at the special chamber session at the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar) on whether the government intends to make the Padang Besar-Bukit Kayu Hitam Wang Kelian Corridor a model for the Malaysia-Thailand border economy.
Additionally, the proposed implementation of the Malaysia-Thailand BEZ development will be brought to bilateral negotiations through the Malaysia-Thailand Committee on Joint Development Strategy for the Border Areas (JDS) platform or other appropriate bilateral platforms.
At the same time, Mohd Shahar also welcomed Rushdan’s view that Malaysia should not simply be a transit route for trade between neighbouring countries, but rather play a more active role in dominating the market through value-added activities and downstream product processing.
Among the development initiatives being implemented in the area are the Perlis Inland Port (PIP), the Chuping Valley and the development of Bukit Kayu Hitam, he said.
He said PIP currently handles about 100,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) per year, with the total handling expected to increase to 180,000 TEU per year.
“The development of border areas is among the government’s important agendas to strengthen the regional economy, increase cross-border connectivity and expand trade activities,” he said.
He said the implementation of strategies under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) 2026-2030 focuses on growth and high-value sectors including electrical and electronics, semiconductors, energy transition, digital technology, agro-food, halal products and tourism. — Bernama

Title: Government approves RM19.05b MRL sukuk programme to finance ECRL project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The government has approved Malaysia Rail Link’s (MRL) fifth sukuk programme worth RM19.05 billion to support the financing of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
"The sukuk under this programme will be issued as a United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) sukuk, in line with the sustainable development goals," he said at the Tokenised Sukuk Initiative Ceremony under MRL's Fifth Sukuk Programme, in collaboration with CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, at the ECRL Gombak Integrated Terminal Station today.
Amir Hamzah said the move continues the efforts under MRL's Third and Fourth SDG Sukuk Programmes, further strengthening its commitment to sustainable infrastructure financing. "The ECRL project is a RM52.43 billion project undertaken by the Malaysian government, involving a term loan of RM37.40 billion from the Export-Import Bank of China (CEXIM) at an interest rate of 3.25 per cent, with the remainder financed through sukuk issuances by local banking institutions," he added.
He stated that construction of the ECRL project has reached 98.5 per cent completion for the Kota Bharu-to-Gombak alignment as of October 2026, and has now entered its final phase of preparations ahead of the targeted commencement of commercial operations on Dec 12, 2026. — Bernama

Title: Chow welcomes RM84.3m coastal protection projects as erosion affects 51 Penang areas
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today welcomed the implementation of seven projects worth RM84.26 million to address risks in coastal areas in the state.
He also welcomed the implementation of the Penang Integrated Shoreline Management Plan (ISMP) study, which began in June 2025 and is scheduled for completion in June 2027.
“The findings of the study will guide the state government and relevant agencies in planning development and managing coastal areas, taking into account current conditions and erosion risks,” he said in a statement issued today while referring to a reply to his question in the Dewan Rakyat recently.
He said the seven projects are to be implemented by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) through the Penang Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
According to the reply by Petra minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, the seven projects included three completed projects, two under implementation and two at the pre-implementation stage.
“They include the RM61.24 million project to construct outfalls and coastal erosion prevention structures in Batu Ferringhi and Tanjung Bungah, and the RM10 million project to construct and repair coastal bunds in Bagan Lebai Tahir,” he said.
The total expenditure on these projects as of September this year is estimated at RM16.8 million.
The minister said Petra is also conducting the ISMP study.
According to the ministry, 51 coastal areas in Penang covering 16.3 kilometres were identified as experiencing erosion.
“Of these, seven areas covering 5.6 kilometres were classified as Category One, with erosion rates of between 4.7 and 17 metres a year,” he said.
He said the DID does not have specific annual records of the number of critical coastal erosion incidents for the period from 2020 to 2026 and the available data is based on the National Coastal Erosion Study (NCES) 2015.
The NCES 2015 identified and assessed the extent of coastal erosion throughout the country.
The study classified coastal erosion into three categories based on the rate of shoreline retreat, the extent of erosion and its impact on the affected areas.
Category One is critical erosion, involving shoreline retreat of more than four metres a year, usually in areas with residents, economic activities, infrastructure and public facilities.
Category Two is significant erosion, with a retreat rate of more than one metre but less than four metres a year, while Category Three is erosion that is not yet serious, with a retreat rate of less than one metre a year.

Title: Two ex-THP Bina senior executives deny CBT-related charges over RM72,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Two former senior executives of a construction company pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to three amended charges of criminal breach of trust (CBT) and abetment involving RM72,000 in penalty proceeds for a proposed office complex in Putrajaya.
Former THP Bina Sdn Bhd health and safety manager Nasahruddin Ahmad, 56, and former TH Properties Sdn Bhd deputy general manager Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, 55, who also served as THP Bina Sdn Bhd deputy general manager, entered their pleas after the charges were read out before Judge Rosli Ahmad.
THP Bina Sdn Bhd is a wholly-owned subsidiary of TH Properties Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Lembaga Tabung Haji, that focuses on construction and project management.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Irna Julieza Maaras told the court that the three charges against both men had been amended.
The amendments involved replacing the phrase “by depositing the money into Nasahruddin’s account” with “by not handing over the money to THP Bina Sdn Bhd” across all three charges.
According to the amended charges, Nasahruddin, in his capacity as the company’s health and safety manager, was entrusted with RM72,000 in penalty proceeds collected from contractor Fourth Wave Sdn Bhd. He is accused of committing CBT by not handing over the money to THP Bina Sdn Bhd.
The penalty proceeds were linked to the proposed development of an office complex in Precinct 3, Federal Territory of Putrajaya, comprising several office floors in Blocks A, B, C and D, an auditorium, and an underground car park for THP Bina Sdn Bhd.
He allegedly committed the offences at Kompleks Islam Putrajaya in Precinct 3 between April 26, 2013, and Aug 12, 2015. The charges, framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, carry a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Meanwhile, Tengku Kamarolhisham faced three amended charges of abetting Nasahruddin by instructing him not to hand over the money to THP Bina Sdn Bhd at the same place and time. The charges were framed under Section 109 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 409 of the same code.
Lawyer Fahmi Abd Moin represented both accused during today’s proceedings, while the court set Dec 17 for mention to submit documents. — Bernama

Title: Court shuts down DNAA bid by trio in Kepong bak kut teh assault case
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 16 — Three men charged with attacking a patron at a bak kut teh restaurant in Kepong will proceed to trial after the Sessions Court today rejected their bid for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA).
According to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT), the application was filed by Wong Weng Luen, Lai Kae Bin and Wan Ken Fei, whose lawyers argued that the prosecution had yet to provide the documents required for trial preparation.
Judge Noor Aini Yusof subsequently directed the prosecution to furnish the outstanding documents to the defence before Jan 5, 2027, describing it as a final opportunity to do so. The judge said trial dates would be set next year.
The prosecution opposed the DNAA application, with deputy public prosecutor Adibah Iman Hassan informing the court that the investigating officer was still compiling the relevant documents.
Wong, Lai and Wan face a charge of causing hurt with a dangerous weapon to Andrew Teh Tiek Hua at a restaurant on Jalan Kepong, Metro Prima, at 2am on May 7.
The offence is framed under Section 326 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years upon conviction, as well as a fine and whipping.
Wong and Wan have remained in custody since they were charged in May after being denied bail. Lai is also being held on remand as he was unable to post the RM20,000 bail amount set by the court.

Title: Thunderstorm warning issued for KL, Selangor and much of Malaysia until evening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a thunderstorm warning for several states across Peninsular Malaysia as well as parts of Sabah and Sarawak, with the alert remaining in effect until 6pm.
MetMalaysia said thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected in Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor.
In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
Affected areas in Pahang are Rompin and Bera.
In Sarawak, the warning includes parts of Miri, Sri Aman, Kapit, Mukah, Sibu, Bintulu, Sarikei, Limbang and Betong, while in Sabah it covers parts of the Interior, West Coast and Tawau divisions, as well as Labuan.
The warning was issued at 3.20pm.

Title: Court fines company owner RM100,000 for letting accounts be used to receive illegal funds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — An owner of a machinery maintenance company was fined RM100,000 by the Sessions Court here today for allowing an individual to use his company’s bank accounts to receive RM190,000 in illicit funds last year.
Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad handed down the sentence to Kong Chon Tin, 32, after he pleaded guilty to three charges. The court also ordered him to serve 36 months in prison if he failed to pay the fine.
Kong was charged with being directly involved in transactions involving RM190,000 belonging to a bank, through the unlawful use of two company accounts belonging to SKD Technology & Service and Akita Machinery & Service at a bank branch along Jalan Klang Lama on Nov 2 and 3, 2025.
The charges were framed under Section 424C(1) of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between three and 10 years, a fine of between RM10,000 and RM150,000, or both, upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, Kong had agreed to allow an individual to use the two company bank accounts to receive funds purportedly derived from gambling activities.
In return, he was promised a five per cent commission on every sum deposited into the accounts. Investigations revealed that he had received and facilitated the deposit of RM190,000 into the two accounts.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Shukor Abu Bakar urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, stressing that the offence involving the misuse of bank accounts was serious and should not be taken lightly, particularly given the amount involved.
“The prosecution requested that the court take into account that a bank is a financial institution and that this matter should be viewed seriously as it involves the public interest, public confidence in financial institutions and the country’s banking system,” he said.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Shukor Abu Bakar urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, stressing that the offence involving the misuse of bank accounts was serious and should not be taken lightly, particularly given the amount involved.
“The prosecution requested that the court take into account that a bank is a financial institution and that this matter should be viewed seriously as it involves the public interest, public confidence in financial institutions and the country’s banking system,” he said.
However, defence counsel Lim Yoi Ping, representing Kong, sought a fine, citing his client’s family responsibilities, lack of previous criminal convictions and remorse over his actions.
“My client currently works part-time as a delivery person. He also cares for his father, who suffers from heart disease and paralysis and requires follow-up treatment at the hospital,” the lawyer said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia pushes for open, inclusive trade system at Apec leaders’ meeting
Article:
SHENZHEN (China), Nov 16 — Malaysia wants the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) to continue playing a role in strengthening an open, transparent, inclusive and rules-based multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) at its core.
Malaysia’s Ambassador to China, Datuk Norman Muhamad, said this has become increasingly important amid global economic uncertainty, which requires more stable international cooperation to ensure continued growth in trade and investment. Malaysia hopes Apec can strengthen trade and financial institutions while ensuring that member economies do not adopt protectionist trade measures that could undermine the global economic recovery, he added.
“What we need now is a more stable framework for international cooperation. As we know, the world is currently facing an uncertain situation that can change suddenly. We hope that, through Apec, we can return to a system that strengthens financial and trade institutions through rules-based relations,” he told an online media briefing ahead of the 33rd Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting.
Norman said Malaysia believes that non-trade and non-economic issues should not divert Apec’s attention from its original purpose as a regional economic cooperation forum. He noted that economic prosperity and future growth would increasingly depend on countries’ ability to leverage emerging developments, including artificial intelligence (AI), logistics and connectivity, while ensuring compliance with international trade rules.
“If we look at the current global situation, prosperity and economic development depend on this new world, including artificial intelligence, logistics, connectivity and compliance with international rules, such as those previously established under the WTO,” he added.
In this regard, Malaysia has outlined seven priority areas that Apec should continue to focus on, including strengthening regional economic integration, facilitating trade and investment, and enhancing connectivity and supply chain resilience. Other priorities include leveraging digitalisation and AI as drivers of productivity and growth through the safe and responsible use of technology, as well as narrowing the digital divide and helping micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) benefit from technological transformation.
Malaysia also wants Apec to continue supporting sustainable and inclusive growth by taking into account the different levels of development and capabilities among member economies, while upholding the principles of consensus, voluntarism and non-binding cooperation within the forum.
Norman said efforts to strengthen regional cooperation should also be supported by Apec’s capacity-building programmes to narrow development gaps among member economies. Malaysia views Apec as an important platform for Asia-Pacific economies to exchange views on trade, trade facilitation, investment, as well as regional and global issues, he added.
Since 2006, Malaysia has benefited from 116 Apec-funded projects with a total approved value of US$12.8 million, in addition to implementing 29 self-funded projects worth US$800,000.
Meanwhile, more than 405,000 travellers, including 20,221 Malaysians, have benefited from the Apec Business Travel Card (ABTC) facility, which facilitates business travel among member economies.
Apec economies are Malaysia’s major trading partners, accounting for 79.7 per cent, or RM2.43 trillion, of the country’s total trade in 2025. Of this amount, Malaysia’s exports to Apec economies totalled RM1.28 trillion, while imports reached RM1.15 trillion.
Apec economies also accounted for RM153.47 billion, or 74 per cent, of the total approved investments across all sectors in Malaysia.
Norman said Malaysia also hopes Apec’s capacity-building programmes will continue to play an important role in helping member economies narrow development gaps and achieve the aspirations of the Apec Putrajaya Vision 2040, which aims to create an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community by 2040.
Commenting on the direction of the upcoming meeting, Norman said Malaysia would continue to work constructively with China and other Apec economies to achieve meaningful, consensus-based outcomes in line with the evolving needs of the regional economy.
The 33rd Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting will be held in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. — Bernama

Title: Johor PKR’s Hassan Karim summoned to Bukit Aman over poem probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim is set to be questioned today over a poem titled
Patik Tak Rela
, which was uploaded to his Facebook account yesterday.
The outspoken politician and activist confirmed that federal police had requested him to appear before the Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) at Bukit Aman here at 3pm today.
“I understand that I will be investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act,” he said when contacted today.
On Saturday, Hassan posted the poem, which touched on what he described as double standards and injustice in Malaysia’s legal system.
The poem is believed to be a response to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest.
Hassan, who is also a lawyer, expressed dissatisfaction over the matter and said he was prepared to face any action taken against him for writing the poem.

Title: Police investigate after vessel crashes into Lumut waterfront seawall
Article:
LUMUT, Nov 16 — Police have confirmed an incident involving a large vessel believed to have struck a seawall near a pedestrian walkway at the Esplanade Wing Lumut Waterfront here after videos of the incident went viral on social media this morning.
Bernama reported that Manjung district police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said police were investigating the incident.
Videos circulating on Threads showed the vessel travelling unusually close to the shoreline before colliding with the structure, leaving part of the seawall damaged.
A Threads user, @mashitahbtbasir, claimed she was in the area before the incident and saw the vessel suddenly accelerate without stopping before the collision occurred.
The user said those at the scene were startled when the vessel failed to stop before colliding with the structure.
Several other users, including @zhoushieng_aman and @irra.izzurin, also shared videos and photographs of the incident on the platform.
It was reported that those at the scene were startled when the vessel failed to stop. — Bernama pic

Title: EV levy among options being considered to speed up charging network rollout, says Miti
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The government is studying various approaches, including the proposed levy on electric vehicles (EVs), to accelerate the development of charging infrastructure towards the targeted 30,000 charging points by 2030, said the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti).
Deputy Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the proposal is still being studied and the government needs to examine various aspects before deciding to implement anything.
He said among the areas requiring attention is the need to expand the capacity of electricity substations, in collaboration with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to facilitate the development of more EV charging stations.
“Without substations, expansion will not be possible. Therefore, we hope TNB can assist the government in providing more EV charging stations and ultimately, it’s in terms of benefits against costs,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Ku Abd Rahman Ku Ismail (PN-Kubang Pasu) on concrete measures taken by the government to achieve the target of 30,000 EV charging points, including ensuring that these facilities are also available in rural areas and small towns.
Sim said that up to Sept 30, 2026, a total of 7,341 public EV charging stations had been installed nationwide, comprising 4,992 alternating current (AC) chargers and 2,349 direct current (DC) fast chargers.
Replying to a question from Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Tun Hussein (BN-Sembrong) concerning efforts to address range anxiety, particularly in rural areas and along highways, Sim said that 148 DC EV chargers are currently operational at rest and service areas (R&Rs), lay-bys and petrol stations along major highways.
He said that 20 charge point operators (CPOs) are actively involved in installing the infrastructure while the government continues to encourage private sector participation without making it mandatory for the operators to install chargers at specific locations.
“Substations are expensive, and TNB needs to plan accordingly. It is not possible to request a substation today and have it ready by tomorrow. It requires construction, planning and other preparations. Therefore, certain areas will require substations.
“We need to ensure that there is sufficient consumer demand to justify the investment costs,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Fresh from Melaka win, Zahid says BN not looking to rush into more elections
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 16 — Barisan Nasional (BN) does not want to rush into holding elections in other states despite its positive performance in several state elections, including the Melaka polls on Saturday.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said, however, that the decision had been left to the respective state leaders to assess whether the time was right to hold elections.
“We have only just concluded the elections in Melaka, so we do not want to rush into holding polls in other states.
“I leave it to the respective Chief Ministers or Menteris Besar to assess the situation and submit their recommendations to the Rulers, as well as advise the respective Rulers and state governors, if they deem it appropriate. However, let us deal with matters one at a time first,” he said.
He spoke at a press conference after officiating at the closing parade of the Wira Muda Negara PLKN (National Service Training Programme) 3.0 Series 4/2026 here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, made the remarks when asked to comment on a proposal by former Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Dr Mohd Puad Zarkashi for state elections to be held in Perak and Pahang, both of which are governed through a BN-Pakatan Harapan (PH) coalition.
Mohd Puad reportedly said the proposal followed the success of the BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) cooperation formula, which helped both coalitions secure significant victories in the 16th Melaka state election on Saturday.
In the election, BN won 21 of the 28 state assembly seats contested, while PH secured four and PN three. — Bernama

Title: Missing Penang doctor, 74, found dead after going missing off Tanjung Bungah
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 16 — An elderly man who went missing while windsurfing off Tanjung Bungah here yesterday was found dead this morning.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director (Operations and Rescue Division) John Sagun Francis said the body of Dr Khaw Chun Sein, 74, was found washed ashore on rocks near Straits Quay Retail Marina at 9.56am.
“The victim was pronounced dead by a Health Ministry (MoH) medical officer at the scene after his identity was confirmed by a family member. The body was then sent to Penang Hospital,” he said in a statement today.
He said the second day of the search and rescue (SAR) operation began at 9am, covering an area of 94.76 square nautical miles divided into five sea search sectors and one aerial search sector around the victim’s last known location.
Yesterday, the department received an emergency call at 7.42pm from a member of the public reporting that a man had gone missing while windsurfing in waters near the Chinese Swimming Club in Tanjung Bungah. — Bernama

Title: Court throws out Mukhriz’s challenge to RM5m tax bill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 —The High Court here today dismissed Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir’s application to challenge the Inland Revenue Board’s (HASiL) issuance of Notices of Additional Assessment totalling more than RM5 million for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years.
Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that the court accepted the HASiL’s submission that the issues raised should first be determined by the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT) through the statutory appellate mechanism under the Income Tax Act 1967.
“This court accepts the Inland Revenue Board’s submission that all the issues should first be ventilated before the SCIT. The issues are to be determined through the statutory appellate mechanism under the Income Tax Act 1967 (ITA). The court concludes that this application is an attempt to bypass the legally established process.
“The appellant (Mukhriz) has appealed to the SCIT under Section 99 ITA, but there are no exceptional circumstances rendering this judicial review. Therefore, the court found that this application is an abuse of the court process,” he said.
The court also ordered the Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) president to pay RM5,000 in costs to the HASiL, the sole remaining respondent.
On Jan 2, 2025, the High Court granted Mukhriz leave to commence judicial review proceedings following an application filed on Dec 20, 2024.
He had initially named the Director-General of the HASiL, Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Government of Malaysia as the first, second and third respondents, respectively.
However, on July 24, 2025, the High Court allowed Anwar and the government to be removed as respondents, leaving only the Director-General of the HASiL in the proceedings.
In his application, the former Kedah Menteri Besar sought an order to quash the HASiL’s decision to issue additional assessment notices for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years, amounting to RM5,020,707.18, on the ground that the decision was unlawful and unreasonable.
He also sought a declaration that the penalty imposed on him under Section 113(2) of the Income Tax Act 1967 was null and void, and ultra vires. — Bernama

Title: No corruption cases linked to illegal crypto mining in Manjung, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has not recorded any corruption cases involving enforcement officers linked to illegal cryptocurrency mining activities in Manjung, Perak.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said this was based on police intelligence records, despite allegations that electricity supplies to cryptocurrency mining premises had been illegally reconnected after being disconnected.
He said the police viewed allegations of enforcement officers engaging in corrupt practices or abusing their authority seriously, including those involving the illegal reconnection of electricity supplies to cryptocurrency mining operations.
“Any information or complaints regarding possible involvement by the police, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) or local authorities will be examined and investigated. Strict action will be taken if evidence of wrongdoing is found,” he said during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham (PH-Beruas), who claimed that TNB disconnected between 100 and 150 illegal power connections at Bitcoin mining facilities every month, but the electricity supply was reconnected illegally soon after.
Addressing enforcement activities in several areas, Shamsul Anuar said 65 cases had been recorded in Ayer Tawar, Beruas, Kampung Koh, Pantai Remis, Pekan Gurney, Segari and Sitiawan, with 65 raids conducted, 823 machines seized, nine arrests made and three charges filed.
In response to Ngeh’s main question on the factors behind the widespread illegal cryptocurrency mining activities in Manjung and the difficulties in bringing those responsible to justice, Shamsul Anuar said 265 raids had been conducted in the district between 2024 and August 2026, resulting in 43 arrests, with 26 individuals charged in court.
He said the government regarded the activities as a serious concern, as the illegal use of electricity, whether through meter tampering or unauthorised connections, not only caused losses for utility companies but also heightened fire risks and threatened public safety.
He said difficulties hampered efforts to identify the real owners and operators, as well as those profiting from the mining operations.
“These activities typically involve the use of crypto wallets or cryptocurrency platforms operating overseas, making it difficult to obtain ownership information, transaction records and the digital evidence required,” he said.
Responding to a supplementary question from Nurul Amin Hamid (PN-Padang Terap) on the possibility of new laws to tackle illegal cryptocurrency mining, Shamsul Anuar said the Home Ministry would step up enforcement in collaboration with TNB, the Energy Commission, local authorities and the Securities Commission Malaysia.
He said efforts to enhance the legal framework must also involve information and data sharing, as well as cooperation from all parties, since cryptocurrency mining falls under the Finance Ministry’s jurisdiction. — Bernama

Title: Court adjourns Negeri Sembilan Exco suit as parties explore settlement
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 16 —The High Court here was informed today that the parties involved in a constitutional suit filed by 10 former state executive council (Exco) members are in discussions to reach an amicable settlement.
The matter came up for hearing before Judge Roz Mawar Rozain.
Counsel Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun, representing the 10 Exco members (plaintiffs), informed the court that the latest development followed a letter dated November10 submitted by the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim alongside with the 10 Exco members to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal, Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad.
Mohd Hafarizam said discussions were still ongoing and the terms of the proposed settlement had yet to be finalised, as they required instructions and approval from his clients.
“I am not at liberty to disclose what the terms of the settlement are because parties are still negotiating. We will be able to bring it to the court’s attention once we have sat down with the lawyers concerned and obtained proper instruction and approval from my clients,” he said during proceedings here today.
Mohd Hafarizam said he was scheduled to meet his clients and Ismail at noon today to obtain further instructions, noting that the matter involves the palace and also confirmed the authenticity of a Nov 10 letter sent by them.
Counsel Datuk Dr Cyrus Das, for the first defendant (the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary), also confirmed that several proposals put forward by the plaintiffs and the Menteri Besar were being considered by the defendants as well as Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
He said he agreed that a brief adjournment should be granted to allow all parties to consider whether the proposals were acceptable and could be implemented.
Following the update, Roz Mawar adjourned the proceedings to Wednesday at 9 am via Zoom to allow parties to finalise the settlement terms.
“I’m mindful of the need to afford all parties a fair and reasonable opportunity to advance their respective position, the proceedings also must be conducted with due regard to the efficient administration of justice.
“These court processes are intended to facilitate fair and orderly resolution of disputes. So they ought not to be utilised, whether directly, indirectly, you know, as a means of exerting pressure upon any party or prolonging a dispute unnecessarily,” said the judge.
The court today was scheduled to hear a preliminary objection by the defendants, who are challenging the use of an originating summons (OS) in the case concerning the revocation of the appointments of the 10 former Exco members.
The 10 former Exco members had filed the OS seeking an interpretation of the State Constitution and named the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary and the state government as defendants, while the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) was granted leave to intervene in the suit and named as third defendant.
The plaintiffs were also represented by counsel Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun, Datuk Syed Faisal Al-Edros Syed Abdullah, Norhazira Abu Haiyan and Muhammad Luqman Hakeem Abas, while the first defendant was also represented by Abdul Rashid Ismail, Siti Nurani Md Zahidi and Diong Pei Jing.
Counsel Razlan Hadri Zulkifli, Marisa Regina Mohd Aris Rizal and Muhammad Yazid Mohamad Salim acted for the state government, while the DKU was represented by counsel Steven Thiru, David Mathew, Shafrin Halim and Gurjeevan Singh.
Two days ago, the media reported that Ismail had confirmed the withdrawal of the contents of a letter submitted to the Malay Rulers dated Sept 17 as well as the position previously taken by members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco).
The letter stated that Ismail, together with 10 Exco members, had unanimously decided to retract the contents of a letter dated September 17. — Bernama

Title: Govt commits RM10.6m to Long Lellang STOLport safety works after fatal Flying Doctor Service crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The government has allocated RM10.615 million to upgrade infrastructure and facilities at the Long Lellang short take-off and landing airport (STOLport) in Sarawak to improve operational safety after a helicopter crashed and caught fire last September.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the estimated resurfacing costs were RM7.191 million for the runway, RM1.2 million for the aircraft parking apron and RM224,000 for the taxiway, while building a mini batching plant would cost RM2 million.
He told the Dewan Rakyat during question time today that resurfacing was expected to begin in 2027 and be completed in the first quarter of 2028.
Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar) had asked what steps the ministry was taking to improve safety management and emergency response at all STOLports in Sarawak following the crash.
Five people, including four Health Ministry medical personnel, died in the Sept 8 crash involving a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter.
Hasbi said the STOLport would also receive a rapid intervention vehicle (RIV) worth RM1.2 million to improve its emergency response capability.
He said the vehicle’s size and capabilities suited the rescue and firefighting needs of a small airport and that one unit was sufficient to meet the standards set out in Civil Aviation Directive 14.
Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) plans to recruit 15 staff in stages to strengthen operations and safety, starting with an airport manager, two technicians and one operations staff member in June 2027, he said.
The company plans to recruit seven airport fire and rescue personnel and four aviation security personnel in December 2027.
He said one aviation security officer and five members of the Malaysia Volunteers Corps (RELA) currently handle security and emergency duties at Long Lellang STOLport.
On Mohamad Shafizan’s question about Bebuling STOLport in Sarawak, Hasbi said the state government had jurisdiction over the airport, its infrastructure was complete and flight tests had been conducted.
“However, we are still waiting for applications for certification by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and for an aerodrome operating licence,” he said.
Meanwhile, replying to Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) on the action taken by the ministry following the Long Lellang crash, he said FDS helicopter operations had not been suspended because the aircraft had undergone airworthiness testing by CAAM.
Hasbi said the helicopter involved held valid certificates of registration and airworthiness and had been confirmed airworthy at take-off.
“The investigation is continuing, and a final report on the accident must be prepared within a year. All the equipment involved, including the engine, has already been sent overseas for laboratory examination,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Selangor moves to curb Bukit Raja flash floods with new pump system
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 16 —- Three high-capacity pumps have been installed near the Bukit Raja interchange in Klang to mitigate the risk of flash floods, which frequently affect the area, the State Assembly was told today.
Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said the immediate measure was expected to help prevent a recurrence of flooding, particularly around the nearby i-City interchange.
“The area is in a valley, where water from the Wyndham Acmar Hotel area accumulates in front of i-City. We completed the installation of the pumps this morning, hoping to resolve the flooding issue at the Bukit Raja interchange,” he said in reply to Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali (PN-Hulu Kelang), who asked about the state government’s efforts to address flash floods on roads across Selangor, during Question Time.
Izham also said several locations with faulty scupper drains had been identified, with the defects contributing not only to flash floods but also to road damage.
“During post-rain inspections, we found hundreds of spots where water had accumulated despite the drains remaining empty. We are taking steps to rectify these faulty scupper drains,” he said.
Yesterday, media reports said more than an hour of continuous heavy rain had caused flash floods along roads around i-City and Section 7, disrupting traffic. — Bernama

Title: PAC raises concerns over policy, project continuity after Loke resignation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 16 — The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today expressed concern over the potential impact of Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s resignation on policy continuity and major infrastructure projects, warning that political leadership transitions must not disrupt governance or delay critical transport initiatives.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said any political change must not paralyse decision-making processes, slow down Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd’s (MAHB) post-privatisation operational transformation agenda, or derail the implementation schedules of high-impact projects.
"The Transport Ministry secretary-general, as the controlling officer, together with the Cabinet, must ensure that governance continuity runs smoothly without any disruption," she told a press conference in Parliament this afternoon.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, resigned as transport minister with immediate effect last Tuesday after the Kuala Lumpur High Court issued a new order allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Abdul Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
At the same time, Mas Ermieyati said the bipartisan committee is also concerned about border enforcement at the country's airports, following the ending of Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain’s secondment as Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) chief.
AKPS is one of the core agencies directly involved in entry-point governance and national airport development, she noted, working alongside the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, the Immigration Department, and the Office of the Chief Government Security Officer (CGSO).
Citing cross-border smuggling cases, including attempts to smuggle drugs and contraband worth millions of ringgit through international gateways such as the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), she stressed that a leadership vacuum cannot be tolerated.
"The PAC emphasises that any vacancy or disruption in the chain of command at the highest level of AKPS must not be allowed to compromise operational readiness, inter-agency intelligence coordination, or the integrity of border control," she said.
Late last month, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail announced that Shuhaily's secondment was being ended and that he would be returned to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
The transition remains subject to procedural requirements, including the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, who approved his two-year contract appointment in July 2025. The Home Ministry has yet to name a replacement.

Title: Teen girl shot in neck near Ranau river, man arrested
Article:
RANAU, Nov 16 — A 15-year-old girl sustained a severe gunshot wound to her neck in a suspected shooting near Sungai Keliu in Kampung Tinamom at about 8pm on Saturday.
Preliminary police investigations revealed that the victim was at the riverside catching fish and frogs with a male companion, who heard a single gunshot while searching for firewood before finding her injured at the riverbank alongside her grandfather.
She was carried out of the area and taken to Paginatan health clinic at about midnight, where medical personnel lodged a police report at about 3.49am on Sunday after treating her for breathing difficulties before referring her to Ranau Hospital.
Police arrested a 40-year-old man at a house in Kampung Tinamom at about 1.30pm on Sunday to assist in investigations under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder.
Police are seeking a seven-day remand order from Monday to record the suspect’s statement, obtain his fingerprints and photographs, and seize relevant exhibits as investigations continue. — Daily Express

Title: Teen charged over Kuching school axe attack, ordered to undergo psychiatric assessment
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 16 — A 16-year-old male student who allegedly attacked a teacher with an axe at a private school here on October 21 has been charged with three offences – carrying a scheduled weapon, causing hurt to the teacher, and possessing explosives without lawful excuse.
Magistrate Leona Dominic Mojiliu, however, ordered the student to be sent to Sentosa Hospital under Section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code for psychiatric assessment and fixed Dec 17 for mention.
The student appeared in court today to face the three charges, but no plea was recorded.
It is understood that his counsel Wejok Tomik had applied for him to be sent to Sentosa Hospital for a psychiatric assessment, and the court allowed the application.
On the first charge, the boy is accused of carrying a small axe, classified as a scheduled weapon under Item 7 of the Second Schedule of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958, without lawful purpose.
The charge was brought under Section 7(1)(a) of the same Act, which provides for imprisonment of between five and 10 years upon conviction.
On the second charge, he is accused of voluntarily causing hurt to a 42-year-old female teacher using a small black axe.
The offence is punishable under Section 324 of the Penal Code with imprisonment of up to 10 years, or a fine, or caning, or any two of these punishments, upon conviction.
For the third charge, he is accused of possessing explosives without lawful purpose, namely firecrackers and a modified beverage container containing explosive substances.
The charge was brought under Section 8 of the Explosives Act 1957, which provides for imprisonment of up to seven years, a fine of RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
All three offences were allegedly committed at around 7.50am at a private school here last month.
The incident went viral on social media after footage showing a student attacking a teacher with an axe within the school premises was circulated online.
Following the incident, the 42-year-old teacher is reported to have sustained injuries to her left hand and was taken to a specialist hospital for treatment before being discharged.
Police had earlier said statements had been recorded from 38 witnesses to assist with the investigation.
The prosecution was conducted by Sarawak State Prosecution director Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin, together with deputy public prosecutors Nur Nisla Abdul Latif and Abdurrahman Abrar Jarni. — The Borneo Post
